spatial_claims.claim: D lies between B and C on a straight line; BC is the whole and CD the annex of the apotome BD
CD < BC since CD is a part of BC
BC produced beyond C and CM cut off equal to CD, giving collinear order B-D-C-M
DM is bisected at C (since DC = CM = CD)
BD is added to DM in a straight line; rect(BM, BD) + sq(CD) = sq(BC) by 2.6
KH is divided at F so that KF:FH = BC:CD via 6.10
KF > FH follows from BC > CD and the proportion KF:FH = BC:CD

configuration_map: Primary configuration is a line with points in collinear order B---D---C---M. BD is the apotome, BC the whole rational line, CD the annex, CM = CD by construction (1.3), so DM = 2CD bisected at C, and BM = BC + CD. A separate line segment KH is divided at F with KF:FH = BC:CD. All reasoning beyond the initial geometric setup is purely algebraic/proportional: commensurability relations, proportion manipulations, and matching of apotome/binomial order definitions. No triangles, circles, angles, or interior/exterior claims appear.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The geometry is limited to collinear point arrangements (B-D-C-M and K-F-H) whose relative positions are straightforward and never conflict. The application of 2.6 is algebraically verified: rect(BM,BD) + sq(CD) = (BC+CD)(BC-CD) + sq(CD) = sq(BC). The core argument is algebraic/proportional (commensurability and order definitions), with no angle decompositions, no interior/exterior claims, and no complex spatial configurations that could harbor contradictions.
